rule: PRINT-ORIENTATION-PRACTICE.md R1 then R2; the 10/1 pose is the regression floor
decision: Outer face down for both. It is the 10/1 pose with the flat outer side face exactly on the bed: the 10/1 left shell stood 2 deg off that face on an edge (8.8 mm2, tip margin below zero, R1 fail). Both shells now stand on 1228 mm2 at a 47 to 48 deg tip angle. The best other poses stand on about 1 mm2 (R1 fail). The four down-facing hole ends and boss faces per shell are the horn-screw counterbore floors (dia 4.4, about 15.5 to 16 mm above the bed): static screw-head seats on support, as in the 10/1 shells (R2 inference: a rough seat under a screw head still clamps). The pack-screw clearance hole (dia 2.2) prints with a horizontal axis; the guide says to check an M2 passes and open it with a 2 mm drill if not.

KEEP the 10/1 pose. It is a colour-only reprint of a part that printed and assembled in this pose. Both poses pass R1 (59.1 deg on 1369 mm2 against 11.8 deg on 748 mm2). The alternative takes the two rear-centre M2.6 seats off support (R2), but those are static clamp seats under a screw head (R2 inference), it is 18 mm taller and puts 114 mm2 of support on the part. The 10-SURFACE side pose stands at 7.2 deg and would need a brim. The alternative was not sliced (release time box).
